summary: binding.gyp exfiltrates filesystem contents and AWS ECS credentials to webhook.site on npm install
details: The package ships a single binding.gyp whose only target is type 'none' with an action that invokes `node -e` on an inline Node payload. No C/C++ source files are shipped, so the file's only purpose is to run that embedded command via GYP command-expansion when npm implicitly runs `node-gyp rebuild` on install. The inline payload shells out to grep/ls/find across /home/user, /output, /workspace, /root, and /tmp (including a grep for an `HTB{` flag pattern), reads repository files, and queries the AWS ECS credential/metadata endpoints at 169.254.170.2 using AWS_CONTAINER_CREDENTIALS_RELATIVE_URI and ECS_CONTAINER_METADATA_URI_V4. Each result, including temporary AWS task credentials, is POSTed to the hardcoded attacker endpoint https://webhook.site/89bd8fe7-328c-4e6d-970c-4d567b5a48a0. The package name resembles a dependency-confusion / typosquat lure (scoped `@dmangal/*` with an implausibly high version `99999.0.2` designed to win resolution).

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
